pinterest.title: Santorini or Mykonos Wedding: Caldera Cliff Tops or Beaches and Bays
pinterest.description: Choosing between a Santorini or Mykonos wedding is a choice between two settings. Santorini is the caldera, with cliff-top villages on the rim of a volcano and ceremonies facing the water and the sunset. Mykonos is beaches, bays and Mykonos Town, with whitewashed lanes, windmills and Little Venice. Our guide sets both islands side by side on the same terms, with no ranking.

pinterest.title: Santorini vs Mykonos Wedding Venues: Cliff-Top Hotels or Beachfront Resorts
pinterest.description: Santorini wedding venues include cliff-top suite hotels, caldera-view resorts and a winery, from Canaves Oia and Grace Hotel to Santo Wines. Mykonos venues sit on the water, from Santa Marina on Ornos Bay to Mykonos Grand and Saint John on Agios Ioannis, Mykonos Blu on Psarou and the Myconian Collection in Elia. Compare venue types and ceremony settings on each island.

pinterest.title: Santorini or Mykonos Wedding: Ceremony on a Cliff or a Chapel Above a Beach
pinterest.description: The setting decides the island; the ceremony decides the venue. Santorini ceremonies mostly face the caldera from terraces and balconies, and Grace Hotel offers a unity ceremony with black and white volcanic sand. On Mykonos, Santa Marina, Mykonos Grand, Saint John and the Myconian Collection each list a chapel. Decide on a religious, civil or symbolic ceremony before you fall for a chapel.

slides: Santorini or Mykonos for your wedding? Neither island wins. They answer different questions.
Santorini is the caldera: cliff-top villages along the rim of a volcano, with ceremonies that face the water and the sunset.
Mykonos is beaches, bays and Mykonos Town, with whitewashed lanes, windmills and Little Venice at the water's edge.
Santorini venues are cliff-top suite hotels, caldera-view resorts and a winery. Mykonos venues sit on bays and beaches: Ornos, Psarou, Agios Ioannis and Elia.
The ceremony decides the venue. Several Mykonos venues have a whitewashed chapel of their own. Choose religious, civil or symbolic before you fall for one.
Both islands have their own airport, with flights from Athens and Thessaloniki. Ferries can be delayed or cancelled in strong winds, so give guests time to spare.
The Australian paperwork is the same on either island, starting with proof that neither of you is already married, such as a Certificate of No Impediment.
Leaning one way? Send us your dates, guest count and ceremony type, and a Wedded Advisor will talk both islands through with you. Link in bio.
instagram_carousel.caption:
Santorini or Mykonos for your wedding?

Our new guide sets the two islands side by side on the same terms, in the same order. It is a comparison, not a ranking, because the right island depends on the setting you picture, the ceremony you want, the experience you want for your guests and the pace of the week.

Santorini: a terrace on the edge of the caldera, with the volcano across the water. Venues include Canaves Oia, Grace Hotel in Imerovigli, Santo Wines in Pyrgos, Katikies, Andronis and Grand Ambassador Santorini.

Mykonos: a chapel above a beach and a town to wander into after dinner. Venues include Santa Marina on Ornos Bay, Mykonos Grand and Saint John on Agios Ioannis, Mykonos Blu on Psarou and the Myconian Collection in Elia.

One house rule shows why the ceremony comes first: Mykonos Grand states that both partners must be Christian Orthodox for a religious wedding on the hotel premises.

Planning a small wedding or an elopement? Either island works, venue by venue.

Tell us which way you are leaning in a message, with your dates and guest count. Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, works in your time zone and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit. Full guide at the link in our bio.
